title: Choosing honest work
hook: kirat karni means work that harms no one and is done honestly
tomorrow: the stall's scale reads a little heavy. does Simran say so?

segments.voice: Last week ended at the dinner table with Bebe's answer: everyone's pace. Simran's pace now has something new in it. A job.

Saturday, early, and Simran is stacking peaches into a pyramid at a farmers' market stall. Her first real job. Her phone buzzes. It's Dev from her class: easy money. His cousin's shop pays for every five-star review, and you don't even have to go there. Twenty reviews, he writes, and that's more than you'll make all morning, from your couch. Simran looks at her pyramid. Then at the line of people already waiting for the stall to open.
screen: `A PYRAMID OF PEACHES.` → `DEV: EASY MONEY, FAKE REVIEWS.` → `MORE THAN A WHOLE MORNING'S PAY.`

segments.voice: Sikhs have a name for what Simran is weighing: kirat karni, earning a living honestly. It sits beside two others in the Sikh life: naam japna, remembering the Name, and vand chhakna, sharing what you have. And there's a story Sikhs tell about it. Tradition says Guru Nanak, on his travels, stayed with Bhai Lalo, a carpenter who earned his bread with his hands. A rich official, Malik Bhago, held a great feast and was offended that the Guru didn't come. When Nanak did come, the story goes, he took Lalo's plain bread in one hand and Bhago's rich food in the other, and squeezed. From Lalo's bread came milk. From Bhago's came blood. The difference wasn't the menu. It was how the money behind it was made. The Granth says the same thing without the drama. On ang 1245, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: one who eats what he earns by his own work, and gives some of it away, recognizes the path. So clean work isn't about how fancy the job is. It's honest, and it harms no one. Dev's reviews harm every stranger who trusts them. Simran's peaches harm nobody. She types back: no thanks, i'm at the stall. Then she opens the stall to the line.
screen: `KIRAT KARNI: AN HONEST LIVING.` · `LALO'S BREAD, BHAGO'S FEAST.` · `ANG 1245: EARN, THEN GIVE SOME.` · `HONEST, AND HARMING NO ONE.` · then, large: `CLEAN WORK.`

segments.voice: Look at your own hands for the whole sit: the palms, the knuckles, whatever marks your work has left. Bring to mind one honest thing they made, fixed or carried this week, however small, and let that be enough.
Choosing honest work. Kirat karni: earning a living honestly, by work that harms no one.
Your line: clean work. Lalo's plain bread, earned honestly, not Bhago's rich feast. Until tomorrow.

fork.setup: a classmate's side hustle pays well: selling 'guaranteed' answers to next week's test. going by today, what's the question to ask?
options: does it harm anyone who trusts it? then it isn't clean work.
is it against the law? if not, it's fine.
does it pay more than a normal job? then why not.
fork.reveal: kirat karni is work that's honest and harms no one. Lalo's bread over Bhago's feast: what matters is how it's earned.
